subject: english-literature
title: Building the HL Essay
welcome_lead: The HL Essay (1200-1500 words) demands a focused line of inquiry. A strong question and selective evidence carry it.
meta_desc: English Literature: structuring the HL Essay with a focused line of inquiry.
final_note: Focus narrows; depth widens. Choose one question and pursue it.

concepts.def: A precise question that guides the HL Essay's argument.
The essay's central claim, sustained throughout the writing.
Choosing quotations that best support the argument; quality over quantity.
Theoretical or scholarly framing brought into the essay.
The synthesis that ties analysis to the line of inquiry.
The HL Essay must be 1200-1500 words.

walkthroughs.body_html: Avoid yes/no questions. A good line: 'How does Atwood use intertextual allusion to interrogate prophecy in The Penelopiad?'. It signals focus, technique, and a critical claim.
One sharply-analysed quotation beats three undigested ones. Show how the language operates — don't merely cite to prove the event happened.
Don't simply repeat. Show where the argument has arrived and what it now lets you see about the text that the introduction could not.

mcqs.q: Why must students distinguish the narrator from the author?
options: It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
The narrator is a constructed voice within the text; the author is the real person who created it. Conflating them misreads irony, unreliable narration and persona.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
The narrator's views are always the author's views.

mcqs.q: What is the structural framework of The Canterbury Tales?
options: It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
It is one continuous story told by Chaucer from beginning to end.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
A frame narrative — pilgrims travelling to Canterbury tell stories along the way, allowing Chaucer to juxtapose different voices, genres and social classes.
Iambic pentameter is any line with ten syllables.
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
Iambic pentameter is when every line rhymes.
A line of five iambs (unstressed-stressed syllable pairs), creating a ten-syllable line with the rhythm da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM.
